Activating mutations of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) gene have been utilized to predict the effectiveness of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. The most common EGFR mutations are exon 19 deletion and exon 21-point mutation, which are sensitive to EGFR TKI. However, rare/complex EGFR mutations still exist, data of which are scarce and controversial. Hence, their role in response to standard therapy remains uncertain.

EGFR is an oncogene with a high frequency of activating mutations in nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC). EGFR inhibitors have been FDA-approved for NSCLC and have shown efficacy in patients with certain EGFR mutations. However, only 9% to 26% of these patients achieve objective responses. In our study, we developed an EGFR gene signature based on The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) RNA-seq data of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) to direct the preselection of patients for more effective EGFR-targeted therapy. This signature infers baseline EGFR signaling pathway activity (denoted as EGFR score) in tumor samples, which is associated with tumor sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors and other tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).
